questions.question: Who originally discovered the phenomenon of superconductivity, and in what material?
answers: Walther Meissner in Copper (1933)
Heike Kamerlingh Onnes in Mercury (1911)
Paul Chu in YBCO (1987)
John Bardeen in Lead (1957)

questions.question: Why is YBCO (YBa2Cu3O7-δ) classified as a High-Temperature Superconductor (HTS)?
answers: It operates above the boiling point of liquid helium (4.2 K)
Its critical temperature (Tc ≈ 93 K) is higher than the boiling point of liquid nitrogen (77 K)
It can withstand melting temperatures above 1000 °C without resistance loss
It acts as a superconductor at room temperature (300 K)

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a theoretical 'perfect conductor' (σ → ∞) and an actual superconductor?
answers: A perfect conductor exhibits infinite thermal conductivity, whereas a superconductor has zero thermal conductivity
A superconductor actively expels magnetic fields when cooled below Tc, whereas a perfect conductor only traps whatever field was present
A superconductor follows Ohm's law strictly, whereas a perfect conductor does not
A perfect conductor expels all magnetic flux lines regardless of its initial cooling state

questions.question: What is the volume magnetic susceptibility (χ = M / H) of a material in the complete Meissner state?
According to the BCS theory, which interaction causes the attractive force responsible for Cooper pairs?
answers: Direct gravitational attraction between valence electrons
Electron-phonon (lattice polarization) coupling
Exchange interactions between aligned parallel electron spins
Strong nuclear force between protons and conduction electrons

questions.question: What is the value of the magnetic flux quantum (Φ0) that penetrates each vortex in a Type-II superconductor?
The characteristic depth to which an external magnetic field penetrates into a superconductor is known as the:
answers: Ginzburg-Landau coherence length
De Broglie thermal wavelength
London penetration depth
Skin depth of high-frequency alternating current

questions.question: In the Resistance vs. Temperature (R–T) curve for YBCO, how does resistance behave as the sample cools through Tc = 93 K?
answers: It decreases smoothly following a quadratic polynomial towards absolute zero
It drops abruptly to zero at 93 K and remains zero at all lower temperatures
It oscillates due to quantum Hall resistance plateaus
It spikes upward due to carrier localization and band gap opening
